newsitem.title: UK: Britain's best-selling Sunday paper backs Labour.
newsitem.headline: Britain's best-selling Sunday paper backs Labour.

text.p: Britain's best-selling Sunday newspaper said it was abandoning its traditional support for the ruling Conservatives and would back the opposition Labour party, firm favourites to win the May 1 general election.

The News of the World, which sells around 4.5 million copies a week, is the second newspaper owned by media magnate Rupert Murdoch to abandon the beleaguered government of John Major and throw its weight behind Labour leader Tony Blair.
"We back Blair, the man for the new millennium" declared the newspaper in its front page headline, saying Major was no longer fit to rule Britain.
"Britain is crying out for strong and moral leadership. John Major has provided neither," it said in an editorial which was made available to Reuters on Saturday ahead of publication.

News of the World, which backed the Conservatives at the last three elections, branded Major a weak man incapable of preventing a series of sleaze scandals and Conservative splits over policy towards Europe.
"His inability to make crucial decisions on Europe has irreparably divided the party," the paper said.
"His weakness at dealing with infighting and political sleaze has brought nationwide contempt for a man who is simply incapable of being prime minister."
The Sun tabloid, Britain's best-selling daily paper, announced earlier in the six-week election campaign that was backing Labour.
News of the World editor Phil Hall said the newspaper felt it was time for a change.
"One in four of the electorate read the News of the World. We've always been a very strong Tory newspaper for the last three campaigns," he told Murdoch-owned Sky television.
"But we've done our own polls: we did a poll among young people and something like 65 percent were backing Blair and only 25 percent were backing Major."
